title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page continues the Proposition on p.354. G is a twisted form of GL(2) over a base S, so G = M^* for a rank-4 Azumaya algebra M (End(F) locally). rho and sigma are invertible ('régulières') sections of G. The page sets eps0 = -sigma^{-1}rho and eps1 = -rho sigma^{-1}, so that eps1 = sigma eps0 sigma^{-1}. The Proposition lists equivalent conditions:
(a) eps0 is regular unipotent, and eps0, eps1 are pointwise 'independent' (N0, N1 are nowhere homothetic).
(b) det sigma = det rho, Tr(sigma^{-1}rho) = -2, and u := Tr(sigma+rho) is invertible.
(c) det sigma = det rho, det(sigma+rho) = 0, and Tr(sigma+rho) is invertible.
(d) sigma+rho = uP, with P an elementary (rank-one) projector.
This page adds two normal-form conditions.
(e) There is an isomorphism phi: GL(2) -> G with phi^{-1}(eps1) = [[1,0],[1,1]] and phi^{-1}(eps0) = [[1,a],[0,1]]. The marginal NB says phi is unique.
(f) There is a (unique) phi with phi^{-1}(rho) = [[0,u],[v,w]] and phi^{-1}(sigma) = [[0,u'],[v',w']], where u+u' = v+v' = 0 and w+w' = u. Then sigma+rho = uP with P = diag(0,1), as in (39).
The margin (37) identifies the entries: u = Tr(sigma+rho) = -u', w = Tr rho, w' = Tr sigma, and -uv = det rho = det sigma. So the entries are dictated by intrinsic invariants of (rho, sigma). Since u and det are invertible, v is invertible.
The matrix entry a is then a = u/v, as in (38). Check: sigma^{-1}rho = (-1/uv)[[w',u],[v,0]][[0,u],[v,w]] = [[-1, -(w+w')/v],[0,-1]], so eps0 = [[1,u/v],[0,1]]. Similarly rho sigma^{-1} = [[-1,0],[-(w+w')/u,-1]], so eps1 = [[1,0],[1,1]].
Uniqueness holds because the common centralizer of two independent unipotents is the center. The quantity u/v = Tr(eps0 eps1) - 2 is the only invariant of the pair; it is the classical trace coordinate of a pair of parabolics.
Proof of (b) <=> (c). For 2x2 matrices, det(1+X) = 1 + Tr X + det X. Hence det(sigma+rho) = det sigma + det rho + det sigma * Tr(sigma^{-1}rho). Under det sigma = det rho this gives (40): det(sigma+rho) = det sigma * (2 + Tr sigma^{-1}rho). This vanishes iff Tr(sigma^{-1}rho) = -2.
Purpose. This is part of 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. It normalizes pairs of 2x2 generators whose 'loop' elements eps0, eps1 are independent parabolics, like the monodromy at cusps of P^1 minus 3 points or modular-type groups. The aim is to coordinatize the space of such (rho, sigma) by u, v, w, then normalize u = 1 on the next page.
errors: The relations in (36) as transcribed ('uv' = vw' = 0') would be wrong. The handwriting reads u+u' = v+v' = 0, which is what sigma+rho = uP with P = diag(0,1) requires. Under that reading everything is consistent.
Notational overloading: u is both the matrix entry of phi^{-1}(rho) and Tr(sigma+rho). This is consistent only because w+w' = u. Harmless.
In (35) the upper-right entry of phi^{-1}(eps0) was left as '?' and is supplied as u/v in (38). It is not 2 in general.
Implicit: v must be invertible for (38). This follows from det rho = -uv being invertible (rho regular) together with u invertible. It is not stated explicitly.
